title: The Nawab appeals to the Khalsa's mercy

blocks.text: The Nawab tries a new line of argument by invoking Sikh teaching about collective prayer and saintly compassion. He repeats that wherever five Singhs prayed together with folded hands, divine authority was present among them.

He also cites scriptural language to argue that even one who has wronged a saint may still be forgiven if the saint so wills it. On that basis he begs the Khalsa to prove the truth of Gurbani through a public act of mercy.

The page therefore turns his petition into a theological appeal rather than a merely political one. He asks not for restored honor, but simply for release from agony, even if death follows immediately after.
